title: GTA 6 hands you a criminal specialty and a very bad alibi
dek: Vice City has a job for you. Twelve questions about how you'd actually pull it off, and what you'd tell the police afterwards.

questions.prompt: Your first job in the city is:

options.label: Driving something that isn't technically yours
Sitting in a van with a laptop and no windows
Standing outside a door, being large
Talking your way past a receptionist who has questions
The road was blocked and nobody checked
Somebody's badge didn't scan
Someone talked, and it wasn't you
The building is somehow still standing

questions.prompt: In the crew, you'd rather be:

options.label: The person nobody sees until it's already done
The person everybody sees and cannot stop
A quiet street where nobody asks questions
options.alt: A quiet residential street of houses

options.label: An empty unit with one very good chair
options.alt: A bare, brightly lit laboratory space

options.label: A neon block with a doorman who knows you
options.alt: A city street lit by neon signs at night

options.label: A dock where the water does the paperwork
options.alt: A wide river running past a quiet bank

questions.helper: Across: quiet or loud. Up: on the ground or buried in paperwork.

questions.prompt: Rank what the job actually needs.
questions.helper: First place is the thing you refuse to go without.

items.label: A contact who owes you a favour
A truck with the right plates

questions.prompt: The brief, as you'd write it.
questions.helper: Two gaps. The crew will fill in the rest badly.
questions.template: The job needs {a}, and afterwards we {b}.

options.label: a driver who doesn't brake
someone inside the cameras
a very large friend at the door
a name that checks out
are gone before the sirens finish
delete the last four hours
let the building explain itself
split it four ways and never call again

questions.prompt: I'd rather end it from a rooftop than walk in the front door.
questions.low: I want to be in the room
questions.high: I want the room in my scope

questions.prompt: A good story gets you further than a good right hook.
The best crimes are quiet and nobody gets hurt.
Your cut, in the end, is:

options.label: A car with no history and a full tank
A folder of things that never happened
A crate that is not on the manifest
Nothing, because you spent it on the job

questions.prompt: When they finally ask, your alibi is:

options.label: "I was driving. Check the cameras, they'll agree."
"I was at work. Ask anyone with a badge I made."
"I was nowhere near it, and I can prove the nowhere."
"I was with you. Remember? You bought the drinks."

results.name: THE WHEELMAN
results.tagline: Three exits, one hand on the wheel
results.blurb: You are calmest at eighty miles an hour with somebody shouting directions that are already wrong. Your plan is a route, your backup plan is a different route, and your emergency plan is a third route nobody has seen yet. Everybody else gets to be brave because you keep the engine running.
results.watchOut: You'll drive anywhere for anyone who asks nicely. Ask where first.

results.name: THE GHOST IN THE WIRES
results.tagline: You were already inside before they locked up
results.blurb: You solve problems with patience and a second monitor. Nobody sees you do the work, and then the door opens, the cameras loop and the alarm forgets why it was ringing. You find it mildly insulting when a job needs a person with a gun.
results.watchOut: Not everything is a system. Some things are just people, and they need a phone call.

results.name: THE FIXER
results.tagline: You know a person for that
results.blurb: You have never carried anything heavier than a folder, and you have never once needed to. Your phone contains a rolodex of people who owe you small, specific favours, and you know exactly which one to spend on a Tuesday. The job is not the crime. The job is the scheduling.
strengths: Keeps the whole crew on the same page
results.watchOut: All that planning can look a lot like never actually doing anything.

results.name: THE ENFORCER
results.tagline: The plan has a door and you are it
results.blurb: You are the reason the crew sleeps well. Somebody has to stand in a hallway looking like a bad outcome, and you do it with a patience that surprises people. You are gentler than you look, which is saying something, because you look like a locked gate.
results.watchOut: Not every problem is standing in front of you. Some of them are in the room, talking.

results.name: THE CON ARTIST
results.blurb: You have never broken into a building in your life. You have, however, arrived at one with a clipboard, a confident walk and a story about a delivery that is running late. People remember you fondly. That is the problem, and also the entire method.
results.watchOut: The story only works until somebody checks. Somebody always checks.

results.name: THE COURIER
results.tagline: It was already in the car when you got in
results.blurb: You move things quietly between places that should not be connected. Your genius is logistics: the right crate, the right dock, the right hour when the port is half asleep. You have never fired a shot and you have never lost a package, and you intend to keep both streaks.
results.watchOut: You'll carry something for a friend without opening it. Open it.

results.name: THE SHARPSHOOTER
results.tagline: One breath, then a very quiet street
results.blurb: You are patient in a way that makes other people nervous. You pick the rooftop, you watch for forty minutes, and you solve the entire problem with a single decision made at the right moment. Everyone else calls it cold. You call it not missing.
results.watchOut: Distance is safe, but it is also distance. Come down sometimes.

results.name: THE PAPER MAN
results.tagline: You've been three different people since breakfast
results.blurb: Your crime scene is a laminator. Badges, deeds, signatures, a whole second life with a clean credit history — you build the version of the world the job needs, and it holds up under a torch. You are the reason the plan survives contact with a security desk.
results.watchOut: The paperwork is not the point. Do not fall in love with the props.

results.name: THE DEMOLITIONS EXPERT
results.tagline: The plan had a wall in it
results.blurb: You look at a locked door and see a suggestion. Your solution is loud, permanent and deeply satisfying, and it usually works, and the insurance claim is somebody else's problem. You are the reason the crew has a story to tell and a reason to leave town.
results.watchOut: There is usually a quieter way in. Try the handle first.
